clue.text: Holy man almost completed kinky epitaphs — capital things

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent out of shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for completed is dropped

parts.note: something completed is over, finished
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A not-quite-finished saint composing eccentric gravestone inscriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here means of the head (Latin caput), so capital things are hats: the stovepipe hat is the tall cylindrical one Abraham Lincoln wore.
explanation.definitionFit: Stovepipe hats are tall headgear, things worn on the head, which the setter calls capital in its Latin sense of belonging to the head.

clue.text: Go after version of Tosca in formal dress

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow or go after them

indicators.note: a version of something is a different rendering of it, so the opera's name is rearranged

parts.note: the Puccini opera's name, taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A production of Puccini's Tosca performed in white tie and tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailcoats are the long-backed jackets worn for white-tie evening occasions, the most formal of men's dress codes.

clue.text: Excursion: one's taken in a lot of the view

indicators.note: taken in means drawn inside, so the letter for one goes within the other word
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the view word is lost

parts.note: a vista is a view, especially a long one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Describing a trip where someone takes in much of the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', so one is taken in: I goes inside VIST, which is VISTA without its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit can be a short trip or outing to a place, so it matches an excursion.

clue.text: Jury initially not empowered in China

indicators.note: in places the selected letters inside the word for friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a friend

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that follow it

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A jury left without any real power, perhaps in a Chinese court.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country, but the capital is just the start of the sentence: 'china' is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a group of people chosen to judge or decide, and a jury is exactly such a selected group.

clue.text: Inclination to right in European city is a local bias

indicators.note: in puts the inclination and right inside the name of the city

parts.note: the French capital
a tip is a tilt or slope
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political lean to the right in a European capital, described as local prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'a local bias' because the phrase is French, the language spoken in the city of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Parti pris is a French phrase for a preconceived opinion or prejudice, so it is a bias as the locals in Paris would say it.

clue.text: Feature of Roman villa thus represented with a copy

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing something reproduced from an original, as a replica of a Roman villa might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocaust was the Roman underfloor heating system, hot air from a furnace circulating under raised floors of villas and baths.

clue.text: Old rhythm picked up in Korean exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a beat is a rhythm

explanation.surface: An ancient rhythm being adopted in a Korean form of exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a sound signal but in a down entry it means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tae Bo is an aerobic workout drawing on taekwondo, the Korean martial art, mixed with boxing moves.

clue.text: Good topic after burglary: how stressful is this?

indicators.note: after places the good-and-topic pair behind the burglary word, so the clue's word order is flipped

parts.note: a break-in is a burglary
G is the abbreviation for good
a point is a topic for discussion

explanation.surface: Someone finds a good subject in a burglary, and wonders how stressful it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question whose answer is the limit of stress someone can take.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaking point is the moment where pressure becomes too much, so it answers how much stress causes collapse.

clue.text: Second nobleman beginning to rule in my homeland

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the letters of the next word

parts.note: taken as written, the outer shell

indicators.note: beginning to signals just the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a second option is the other one
a count is a European noble
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A second-rank aristocrat starting to govern in the speaker's native land.
explanation.walkthrough: M and Y go round OTHER, COUNT and R. 'Second' looks like a time abbreviation but means other.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother country is a phrase for the land of one's birth or ancestry, the same idea as a homeland.

clue.text: Limits time in power, overlooking Government crime

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the letter for government is left out

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's period in power
G is the abbreviation for government
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Term limits on rulers that ignore corruption in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or curb, as a rider pulls the reins of a horse, so it means limits as a verb.

clue.text: Opening that is never for supplementary player

parts.note: a rip is a tear or opening
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
no as in not at all, never

explanation.surface: An audition where an opening is never given to a substitute performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripieno is a baroque music term from Italian 'filled up'.
explanation.definitionFit: In a concerto grosso the ripieno players are the extra orchestral performers who fill out the sound behind the soloists.

clue.text: In France, Malbec's served after a second course

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
Côt is the name used for the Malbec grape in south-west France

explanation.surface: A French meal where Malbec is poured after the second course.
explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like part of a dinner but is a racecourse: Ascot, near Windsor, hosts Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, so it is a course in the horse-racing sense.

clue.text: Colin, shivering, reluctant to appear in minimal garment

indicators.note: shivering means shaking, so the letters of the name are shaken up

parts.note: the name, taken as letters to rearrange
loth is unwilling

explanation.surface: Colin, cold and shy, unwilling to be seen in very little clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single strip of cloth around the hips, about as little clothing as one can wear.

clue.text: Turning tense with alarm, mostly unjustified

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards
mostly means not entirely, so the alarm word loses its last letter

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
panic is sudden alarm

explanation.surface: Someone growing nervous and alarmed for no good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, so a remark that is inapt is not warranted or justified.

clue.text: Area taken from lobby — quiet room, largely displaying success

indicators.note: taken from means removed, so the area letter is dropped from the lobby word

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
an atrium is an entrance hall

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the room word loses its last letter

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
a hall is a room

explanation.surface: A quiet hotel foyer and room proudly shown off as an achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphal describes something celebrating a victory, like a triumphal arch, so it shows off success.

clue.text: It produces nothing of note, however plucky you are

definitions.text: It produces nothing of note, however plucky you are

parts.words: It produces nothing of note, however plucky you are
parts.note: surface reading: some endeavour that achieves nothing worth noticing however brave you are

parts.words: It produces nothing of note, however plucky you are
parts.note: setter's reading: an imaginary instrument makes no musical notes no matter how hard you pluck strings that are not there

explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a musical note and 'plucky' means plucking strings, not courage: miming a guitar solo produces no sound at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Air guitar is the mime of strumming an invisible guitar, which by design makes no musical sound however energetic the player.

clue.text: Wise words Miss Oprah broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Oprah Winfrey's sage advice going out on her television show.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphorisms are short pithy sayings expressing a general truth, the kind of wise words quoted as maxims.

clue.text: Own goal perhaps is transfixing half of team in scare

indicators.note: transfixing means piercing through, so these pieces go through the middle of the team letters
half of keeps only two of the four letters of the following word

parts.note: only its first half is kept, the outer shell
an own goal is an example of an error
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football own goal leaves half the team in a state of fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags an own goal as just one kind of mistake, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To terrorise is to frighten someone badly, so it works as the verb scare.

clue.text: Backed flag about minor abuses

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes around the minor word
backed means moved backwards, so the word for flag is read in reverse

parts.note: to flag is to droop or sag
slight means minor or small

explanation.surface: Supporters of a banner causing minor mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning droop.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaslight is to manipulate someone into doubting their own sanity, a form of psychological abuse, so gaslights means abuses.

clue.text: Body temperature, at a rough estimate

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
or so means approximately

explanation.surface: A nurse giving an approximate body temperature reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Has cleverer ideas than vote losers linked to markets

parts.note: those voted out are outs
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: Election losers whose links to trade give them smarter plans.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart someone is to be more clever than they are, beating them with superior thinking.

clue.text: Some orbit it and a satellite

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters are found inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: Spacecraft that circle a moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link, but its first two letters complete the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn, so it is a natural satellite.

clue.text: What regularly rises is rising, doing for cavity

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means going upwards, so the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the sun comes up every morning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that keeps going up repeatedly, doing someone harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but here it just means daily.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow cavity, most commonly one of the air-filled spaces in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Question about including Italy gets key support?

parts.note: QU is the abbreviation for question

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the about word goes around the Italy letter

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An enquiry about whether Italy gets backing on an important matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that key is used loosely: a quoin can be a keystone or a wedge supporting a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoin is an external cornerstone or a wedge-shaped keystone of an arch, so it is a structural support.

clue.text: Abandon importing large quantity of bedding

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the large letter goes inside the abandon word

parts.note: to quit is to give up or abandon
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Giving up on bringing in a large bulk order of sheets and blankets.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt is a padded bed cover, so it is an item of bedding.

clue.text: Marks comments about children

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the comments word goes around the children letters

parts.note: notes are brief remarks or comments
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A teacher's grades and remarks on pupils' work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' looks like school grades, but it is cuts made in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Notches are small V-shaped cuts made as marks, such as tallies scored on a stick.

clue.text: Less quiet? Backed change suppressing volume

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
suppressing means holding down or removing, so the volume letter is taken out

parts.note: a revision is a change or amendment
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: Supporting an alteration that turns down the sound, which oddly makes things louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier means making more sound, the opposite of quiet, so it is the comparative less quiet.

clue.text: Loosely tethers single dog

indicators.note: loosely means not held firmly in place, so the letters can move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tying up a lone dog without much care.
explanation.definitionFit: The English setter is a breed of gun dog with a long speckled coat, trained to point game birds.
